record.title: SpaceX discloses a $1.25B monthly Anthropic compute agreement with a 90-day exit right
record.summary: SpaceX's May 20, 2026 SEC Form S-1 says it entered cloud-services agreements with Anthropic for compute access across Colossus and Colossus II. SpaceX states that Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 after discounted ramp-up fees in May and June 2026, while either party may terminate on 90 days' notice. A June 1 SEC response repeats the stated monthly amount and says SpaceX did not view the contracts as a substantial dependence because capacity and revenue could be redeployed. The filing establishes the issuer's disclosed contract terms, not realized payments, delivered capacity, utilization or a guaranteed three-year spend.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: SpaceX's May 20, 2026 SEC Form S-1 states that it entered cloud-services agreements with Anthropic in May 2026 for compute access across Colossus and Colossus II.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: SpaceX states in its SEC filing that Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with May and June 2026 capacity ramping at a reduced fee; either party may terminate the agreements on 90 days' notice. These are disclosed contract terms, not evidence that each fee has been paid or that the agreement will run through May 2029.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In its SEC response, SpaceX says the agreements are not contracts on which its business is substantially dependent and says it believes capacity and revenue could be redeployed if the agreements end; this is SpaceX's characterization, not an independent measurement of redeployment or the economics to Anthropic.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed disclosures do not establish monthly payments made, exact capacity reserved or delivered, compute utilization, the contract's full conditions and remedies, or the comparative cost and performance of the supplied compute.

evidence_gaps.description: No public record inspected establishes payments made, monthly fee realization, capacity delivery or accelerator-hours used under the Anthropic agreements.
The disclosed contract does not quantify Anthropic's delivered compute share, utilization or comparative unit economics across providers.
The public summary does not disclose full minimum-use, service-level, shortfall, or termination-remedy provisions.

brief.importance_rationale: If the contract continues on the stated terms, a $1.25B monthly fee for frontier-model compute is large enough to affect infrastructure financing, provider allocation and capacity planning. The 90-day termination option, reduced ramp-up fees and absence of realized payment or usage data materially limit what the filing proves.
limitations: The $1.25B monthly fee is an issuer-disclosed agreement term, not evidence of cash paid, full-period realization or a guaranteed three-year contract. May and June 2026 were described as reduced-fee ramp-up months.
Either party may terminate on 90 days' notice. The reviewed excerpts do not specify minimum take-or-pay obligations, detailed service levels, remedies, accelerator-hours or exact capacity allocation.

SpaceX's statements that compute capacity and revenue could be redeployed and that it is not substantially dependent on the agreements are issuer representations, not independent utilization or counterparty-dependence measurements.
No matched workload-level comparison establishes the delivered compute's cost, performance, energy use or reliability relative to other providers.
brief.summary: SpaceX's May 20, 2026 SEC Form S-1 says it entered cloud-services agreements with Anthropic for compute access across Colossus and Colossus II. SpaceX states that Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 after discounted ramp-up fees in May and June 2026, while either party may terminate on 90 days' notice. A June 1 SEC response repeats the stated monthly amount and says SpaceX did not view the contracts as a substantial dependence because capacity and revenue could be redeployed. The filing establishes the issuer's disclosed contract terms, not realized payments, delivered capacity, utilization or a guaranteed three-year spend.

technical.claimed_result: SpaceX disclosed a $1.25B monthly fee through May 2029 for Anthropic compute access, after reduced-fee ramp-up in May and June 2026, with either party able to terminate on 90 days' notice. This is a contractual fee schedule stated by SpaceX, not realized spend.
technical.compute_or_cost: $1.25B/month stated fee through May 2029; May and June 2026 ramp-up fees are reduced. Exact compute quantity, unit price, utilization and payments are not established in the reviewed sources.
technical.demonstrated_result: The SEC filing and staff-comment response are public primary documents. Their existence and wording are directly inspectable; the operational performance, delivered capacity and payments are not independently verified.
technical.mechanism: SpaceX monetizes compute capacity at its Colossus and Colossus II facilities by selling cloud compute services to Anthropic. SpaceX says the agreements permit 90-day termination by either party and that unused capacity could be reassigned to its own initiatives or other customers.
technical.regime: One disclosed provider-customer compute-services relationship at SpaceX facilities in 2026, with a stated monthly fee schedule and 90-day exit right. No general inference about Anthropic's provider mix, total compute demand or supplier dependence follows.
technical.reproducibility: Primary SEC filing and SEC response are publicly accessible. No underlying executed contract, invoices, service logs or independent usage audit was inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: The filing provides no matched supplier or workload baseline. SpaceX's own statement that capacity and revenue could be redeployed is a counterparty representation, not an external comparison.

brief.title: SpaceX discloses a $1.25B monthly Anthropic compute agreement with a 90-day exit right
brief.why_it_matters: A large frontier-compute contract provides a rare public view into the scale and structure of AI infrastructure demand. Its monthly fee, ramp schedule and short termination window together matter for financing and capacity planning; the record does not show realized spend, used capacity or Anthropic's dependence on SpaceX.

related.summary: SpaceX separately reported a compute-services contract with Anthropic. The S-1 reviewed here does not allocate compute utilization or spending to SpaceX, so the two disclosures are related context rather than a supplier-share reconciliation.

other.title: Anthropic’s preliminary S-1 reports rapid growth alongside compute financing exposure
other.summary: Anthropic’s October 26, 2026 preliminary Form S-1 reports $11.6 billion in revenue and $1.0 billion in operating income for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $787 million in revenue and a $1.2 billion operating loss in the same 2025 quarter. The filing says consumption-based services made up 80% of first-half 2026 revenue and 48% of revenue came through cloud-provider marketplaces. It reports $112.4 billion in cash and $19.3 billion in short-term investments at June 30, 2026; the six-month 2026 figures are unaudited. The filing also describes multi-year minimum-purchase and take-or-pay compute obligations, a shift toward leased accelerators and dedicated facilities, and conditional infrastructure financing. The filing describes capacity up to $42 billion under a Broadcom arrangement for 2026 lease obligations, up to $30 billion from Google (none issued by June 30, 2026), and up to $20 billion from Amazon; separately, it reports $10.2 billion aggregate principal of notes issued to two accredited investors by the filing date. These facility ceilings do not establish cash drawn, amounts paid or compute delivered. Several aggregate compute-commitment totals are left blank in the preliminary filing. Large reported net losses include non-cash fair-value remeasurement of convertible notes and related instruments. These disclosures describe the company’s reported results and financing structure; they do not establish compute utilization, future revenue, total realized compute cost or a completed IPO.
